title: Tool-shadow execution surface: deterministic injection, parallel hedging and explicit retry ergonomics
author: Sasha Patel
description:
Background and motivation:
This PR introduces the "tool-shadow" execution surface and ergonomics primitives to improve multi-tool and parallel tool-call behavior when running under the OpenAI-compat API surface. Problems addressed: non-deterministic tool-result injection when several tool calls race, awkward retry semantics that duplicate side-effects, and poor developer control over hedging vs deterministic ordering.

Summary of changes (high level):
- New public option `execution.tool_shadow` (API + SDK) that enables deterministic result injection semantics: tool calls are assigned stable call-ids and results are injected into the LLM output stream only when explicitly committed.
- Hedging/parallelism primitives: `hedge_window_ms` and `hedge_policy` allow callers to spec speculative parallel calls and automatic dedup/fast-path commit when the earliest successful result arrives.
- Explicit retry surface: `retry_metadata` lets the platform attach idempotency tokens, retry count, and side-effect-suppression flags so that infra can safely retry tool-backed calls without duplicating external side effects.
- OpenAI-compat layer: map new primitives to `function_call`/`tool` compat semantics so existing clients can opt-in without changing server-side call semantics.
- Server runtime: scheduler changes to honor call-id affinity and to coalesce KV-cache state for speculative hedged requests to avoid cold-KV duplication.
- Tests/examples: comprehensive unit/integration tests plus two new examples (parallel-search-merge and hedged-qa) demonstrating ergonomics and recommended patterns.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Deterministic injection requires buffering of tool results until a commit decision is reached. We optimized for memory by streaming partial tool logs and only retaining call metadata in-memory.
- Hedging improves tail latency but can increase GPU token work; the optimizer proposes conservative defaults (hedge_window_ms=50) and exposes cost impact in console telemetry.
- Retry metadata is advisory to downstream adapters (e.g., HTTP tool connectors) — strongly recommended to integrate with connector-level idempotency where available (e.g., Idempotency-Key).

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- The OpenAI-compat mapping is opt-in behind the account flag `tool_shadow_opt_in`. We will roll this to 5% of accounts for two weeks and monitor regressions and e2e latency.
- SDK changes include a backwards-compatible optional argument. No breaking changes expected.

Testing and validation:
- Added 42 unit tests and 6 integration scenarios that simulate races, retries, and hedged success/failures.
- Load run against perf-canary: p99 latency for hedged requests improved from 780ms->640ms in our synthetic Q&A workload (with 10% extra GPU token work).

Checklist:
- [x] API design reviewed
- [x] Runtime scheduler changes implemented
- [x] SDK bindings (Python + TS) added
- [x] Integration tests covering failure/retry/commit semantics
- [x] Docs draft in redwood-docs referencing examples
